common_name: Nuccio's Ruby Camellia (Formal Double Deep Red Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Nuccio's Ruby, from the renowned Nuccio's Nurseries breeding program, is prized for perfectly formed deep red double flowers.

directions: Nuccio's Ruby, from the renowned Nuccio's Nurseries camellia breeding program in California, bears formal double flowers in a deep, rich ruby-red, with tightly overlapping petals that hold their symmetrical shape exceptionally well from bud to full bloom, making it a favorite among show exhibitors as well as home gardeners. Like other Camellia japonica cultivars it flowers in winter into early spring on a slow-growing, long-lived evergreen shrub with glossy, dark green foliage that provides year-round structure. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered light, and protect from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind, which can shorten flower life. Prune only lightly right after bloom, since flower buds for the following season set on the current year's growth.

common_name: Margaret Davis Camellia (White with Red Picotee Edge Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Margaret Davis is an Australian-bred camellia famous for its crisp white petals edged in bright red, a distinctive picotee pattern.

directions: Margaret Davis, bred in Australia, is one of the most distinctive camellia cultivars available, bearing semi-double to double flowers in crisp white with a bright, irregular red picotee edge along each petal margin, a striking pattern rarely seen in the genus. It flowers over a long midseason window on a vigorous, well-branched evergreen shrub with the glossy dark foliage typical of Camellia japonica. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered light, and keep soil consistently moist, since camellias struggle in prolonged drought. Prune only right after bloom to shape the plant, since next season's flower buds form on the current year's growth.

common_name: Bob Hope Camellia (Popular Dark Red Semi-Double Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Bob Hope is one of the most widely planted modern camellia cultivars, valued for dark, velvety red semi-double flowers.

directions: Bob Hope is one of the most widely planted and recognized modern camellia cultivars, bearing large, semi-double flowers in an intensely dark, velvety red with an informal, loosely arranged petal pattern that contrasts nicely with the more formal doubles common in the genus. It flowers heavily over a long midseason window on a vigorous, well-branched evergreen shrub with glossy dark foliage. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered light, and protect from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind, both of which can shorten flower life and stress foliage. Prune only right after bloom to shape the plant, since flower buds for the following season form on the current year's growth.

common_name: Kick Off Camellia (Red and White Striped Camellia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Kick Off bears striking red-and-white striped and blotched flowers, with some blooms and even branches showing solid red or solid white.

directions: Kick Off is a novelty camellia cultivar prized for its variable, unpredictable red-and-white striped and blotched flowers, a genetically unstable pattern that means individual blooms, and occasionally whole branches, can appear solid red, solid white, or any combination of striping in between, giving each flowering season a slightly different display. It flowers over a long midseason window on a vigorous evergreen shrub with glossy dark foliage typical of Camellia japonica. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered light, and protect from harsh sun and wind. Prune only right after bloom, since next season's flower buds form on the current year's growth; some growers selectively propagate cuttings from branches showing a favorite color pattern.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Dahlonega, named for the north Georgia gold-rush town, bears formal double flowers with a rare pale gold-yellow tint.

directions: Dahlonega, named for the north Georgia town famous for America's first gold rush, bears formal double flowers in creamy white delicately tinged with pale gold-yellow at the petal base, a subtle warm cast that is unusual among camellias, which rarely show any yellow tones. It flowers over a long midseason window on a vigorous, well-branched evergreen shrub with the glossy dark foliage typical of Camellia japonica. Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to filtered light, and protect from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind. Prune only right after bloom to shape the plant, since flower buds for the following season set on the current year's growth.
